# Keep Workstation's toolbar to Reset, Undo and Redo

## Context

The operator rejected Workstation's expanded topology toolbar on 2026-09-13: Save workspace, Close workspace and per-window Open/Show controls occupy multiple rows and dominate the docking surface. The requested product surface is Reset to default, Undo and Redo. The operator renewed this polish lane on 2026-09-22. The earlier transition parking is lifted for this bounded consumer change; current popup, history and persistence journeys remain its validation gate.

## The Problem

The toolbar grows with every popup because WorkspaceController observes WorkspaceSet membership and creates two recovery buttons per participant. Native window close, automatic transaction persistence and the pane's existing pop-out action already supply the intended interactions; the app should not duplicate those controls across an expanding toolbar.

## The Architectural Reality

At composition draft PR #18677 (`921118d447`), `apps/workstation/view/TopologyToolbar.mjs` owns the static buttons and state readout. `WorkspaceController.syncTopologyBar()` inserts the per-window buttons, and `onComponentConstructed()` subscribes to membership. `Workspace.syncTopologyState()` and its boot/projection hooks exist for the window-count readout. `resources/scss/src/apps/workstation/Workspace.scss` styles that readout.

Automatic persistence already belongs to `TopologyLibrary.attachGroup()`: its Group commit listener calls `persistCurrent()`. Existing persistence/adoption APIs must be distinguished from the toolbar-only handlers before deleting code.

## The Fix

Keep only Reset to default, Undo and Redo in the topology toolbar, including the live history badges. Per the operator's 2026-09-23 composition refinement, render two rows: tour/theme above, live store statistics beside the three layout controls below. Reuse the existing view owners and one consistent background. Remove Save/Close, per-window Open/Show controls and the extra topology readout. Remove their UI-only handlers, membership subscription, readout publisher and unused styling. Preserve reset and live history bindings, normal persistence, native close and pane pop-out. Update the app README, the assertions which encoded the removed UI, and the passages in `learn/guides/uibuildingblocks/DockLayoutsWindows.md` that teach it.

## Contract Ledger Matrix

| Surface | Authority | Behavior | Fallback | Docs | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Topology toolbar | Operator product correction | Exactly Reset to default, Undo, Redo; popup membership adds no controls | Existing disabled states when actions are unavailable | Workstation README | Live screenshots before/after popup creation and unit control-count assertion |
| Existing app workflows | Group persistence and native/pane controls | Persist commits automatically; use native close and pane pop-out | Existing engine refusal/recovery semantics | README | Existing saved-layout and pop-out journeys |

## Decision Record impact

None: bounded consumer presentation correction; no engine or persistence contract redesign.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The topology toolbar contains only Reset to default, Undo and Redo, before and after creating or restoring multiple popup participants. The app has two visual control rows: tour/theme, then stats and layout controls with a consistent skin.
- [ ] Reset restores the declared default; Undo/Redo enabled states and history counts remain reactive and operable.
- [ ] Toolbar-only recovery handlers, membership observation and readout state/style are removed, without deleting APIs still used by boot, persistence or other consumers.
- [ ] Automatic persistence, native close and pane pop-out keep working; no replacement Save/Close/Open surface is introduced elsewhere as part of this change. Native close and cold hydrate retain headless participants; the user-facing recovery is Reset to the shipped arrangement (or Undo while warm history exists). Layout-preserving open/mount remains programmatic. No automatic inline recovery or window-lifecycle policy change is included.
- [ ] README, relevant tests and `learn/guides/uibuildingblocks/DockLayoutsWindows.md` describe the corrected UI. The guide teaches the per-window `Open … as window` / `Show … here` buttons in stations two and three, **Show here** as a road home in station five, and popups offering themselves as windows in station six. A live main-window screenshot with at least two popups demonstrates that toolbar height no longer grows with membership.

## Out of Scope

Multi-window transition repair (higher priority), engine changes, deleting storage/recovery APIs merely because their toolbar buttons disappear, or a broader visual redesign beyond the requested two-row composition.

## Avoided Traps

Do not hide the same buttons in an unsolicited menu, replace them with icons, or retain a membership-driven hidden subtree. Do not mistake removing manual-save UI for removing automatic persistence. Do not turn this deferred correction into a blocker for the transition repair.
